publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: A nationwide survey of psychological distress among Chinese people in the COVID‐19 epidemic: implications and policy recommendations

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: peritraumatic psychological distress in the Chinese general population during the first weeks of the COVID-19 epidemic - measured by an index built for the occasion
span.quote: A self-report questionnaire was designed to survey peritraumatic psychological distress during the epidemic. Data collection began on 31 January 2020, the day when the WHO announced the Novel Coronavirus Pneumonia of China as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

span.label: how prevalent and how severe the distress was, and which groups carried most of it
span.quote: Almost 35% of the respondents experienced psychological distress (29.29% of the respondents’ scores were between 28 and 51, and 5.14% of the respondents’ scores were ≥52).

span.label: the first nationwide distress survey of the epidemic, 52,730 responses, and a new instrument - the COVID-19 Peritraumatic Distress Index
span.quote: This study received a total of 52 730 valid responses from 36 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities, as well as from Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan by 10 February 2020. Among all the respondents, 18 599 were males (35.27%) and 34 131 were females (64.73%).

span.label: existence
span.quote: Almost 35% of the respondents experienced psychological distress (29.29% of the respondents’ scores were between 28 and 51, and 5.14% of the respondents’ scores were ≥52).

span.label: a population-scale distress signal during a quarantine, varying by sex, age, education, occupation and region
span.quote: It is noteworthy that migrant workers experienced the highest level of distress (mean (SD)=31.89 (23.51), F=1602.501, p<0.001) among all occupations. The concern about virus exposure in public transportation when returning to work, their worries about delays in work time and subsequent deprivation of their anticipated income may explain the high stress level.

span.label: self-report questionnaire distributed by QR code through an online assessment platform, open to the general public, from the day the WHO declared a PHEIC
span.term: self-report questionnaire distributed by QR code through an online assessment platform, open to the general public, from the day the WHO declared a PHEIC
span.quote: Leveraging the Siuvo Intelligent Psychological Assessment Platform, we presented QR codes of the questionnaire online openly accessible to the general public nationwide.

span.label: the explanations offered are all social rather than clinical - information exposure for the young, morbidity risk for the elderly, transport and lost income for migrant workers, health self-awareness for the educated - and every one is hedged in the authors' own words
span.quote: It is noteworthy that migrant workers experienced the highest level of distress (mean (SD)=31.89 (23.51), F=1602.501, p<0.001) among all occupations. The concern about virus exposure in public transportation when returning to work, their worries about delays in work time and subsequent deprivation of their anticipated income may explain the high stress level.

span.label: the decline over time is attributed to the government's control measures, alongside the observation that the lowest point fell on a festival - two candidate causes for one curve, neither separated from the other
span.quote: Results also indicated that as time passes, distress levels among the public have been significantly descending, with the lowest distress level during the Lantern Festival (8 February).

span.label: THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE THE SURVEY. The CPDI was `DESIGNED` for this epidemic and fielded from `31 January 2020, THE DAY WHEN THE WHO announced` the PHEIC - built, validated and deployed inside the window it measures
span.quote: A self-report questionnaire was designed to survey peritraumatic psychological distress during the epidemic. Data collection began on 31 January 2020, the day when the WHO announced the Novel Coronavirus Pneumonia of China as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

span.label: AND ITS CUT-OFFS ARE ASSERTED RATHER THAN DERIVED: `A score between 28 and 51 indicates mild to moderate distress. A SCORE >= 52 INDICATES SEVERE DISTRESS.` No derivation, no comparison against an existing scale, no ROC analysis
span.quote: A score between 28 and 51 indicates mild to moderate distress. A score ≥52 indicates severe distress.

span.label: the validation offered does not address the threshold: content validity by psychiatrists, and a Cronbach's alpha of 0.95, WHICH IS AN INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY STATISTIC AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHERE A CUT-OFF SHOULD SIT
span.quote: Psychiatrists from the Shanghai Mental Health Center verified the content validity of the CPDI. The Cronbach’s alpha of CPDI is 0.95

span.label: the sample is self-selected through QR codes on an online platform `openly accessible to the general public`, and it is 64.73% female against a population near 49% - a skew the paper reports and does not adjust for
span.quote: Leveraging the Siuvo Intelligent Psychological Assessment Platform, we presented QR codes of the questionnaire online openly accessible to the general public nationwide.

span.label: THE PAPER CARRIES NO LIMITATIONS SECTION AT ALL. It ends on four policy recommendations. For a 1,156-word letter that is a fact about the genre rather than about the authors, and it is why the caveats above had to be read out of the methods
span.quote: This study received a total of 52 730 valid responses from 36 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities, as well as from Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan by 10 February 2020. Among all the respondents, 18 599 were males (35.27%) and 34 131 were females (64.73%).

span.label: the regional comparison uses Shanghai as a case where high exposure risk did NOT produce high distress, and attributes the difference to the public health system
span.note: eliminates: exposure risk alone as the explanation of the regional pattern - the paper names a case that cuts against it and offers a mechanism · outcome: held
span.quote: The distress level is not spiking. This is probably because of the fact that Shanghai has one of the best public health systems in China.

span.label: whether the CPDI cut-offs correspond to anything outside the CPDI
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the validation is content validity and internal consistency, neither of which addresses where the threshold sits · outcome: failed
span.quote: A score between 28 and 51 indicates mild to moderate distress. A score ≥52 indicates severe distress.

span.label: whether the respondents represent the population the prevalence is quoted for
span.note: eliminates: nothing - recruitment was by open QR code and the sample is 64.73% female; the skew is reported and not adjusted for · outcome: failed
span.quote: Leveraging the Siuvo Intelligent Psychological Assessment Platform, we presented QR codes of the questionnaire online openly accessible to the general public nationwide.

span.label: CPDI
span.quote: the COVID-19 Peritraumatic Distress Index (CPDI) inquired about the frequency of anxiety, depression, specific phobias, cognitive change, avoidance and compulsive behaviour, physical symptoms and loss of social functioning in the past week, ranging from 0 to 100.

span.label: content validity
span.quote: Psychiatrists from the Shanghai Mental Health Center verified the content validity of the CPDI. The Cronbach’s alpha of CPDI is 0.95

span.label: peritraumatic psychological distress
span.quote: A self-report questionnaire was designed to survey peritraumatic psychological distress during the epidemic. Data collection began on 31 January 2020, the day when the WHO announced the Novel Coronavirus Pneumonia of China as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

span.label: psychological distress - AS OPERATIONALISED HERE, A SCORE ABOVE 28 ON A SCALE THAT DID NOT EXIST TEN DAYS EARLIER. The headline `almost 35% of the respondents experienced psychological distress` IS THAT THRESHOLD, restated as a prevalence, and the prevalence is what 4,481 papers cite
span.quote: Almost 35% of the respondents experienced psychological distress (29.29% of the respondents’ scores were between 28 and 51, and 5.14% of the respondents’ scores were ≥52).

span.label: CPDI - a 0-100 index over anxiety, depression, specific phobias, cognitive change, avoidance, compulsive behaviour, physical symptoms and loss of social functioning in the past week. EIGHT DOMAINS COLLAPSED INTO ONE NUMBER, and the number carries the diagnosis
span.quote: the COVID-19 Peritraumatic Distress Index (CPDI) inquired about the frequency of anxiety, depression, specific phobias, cognitive change, avoidance and compulsive behaviour, physical symptoms and loss of social functioning in the past week, ranging from 0 to 100.

span.label: the validation - CONTENT VALIDITY plus alpha 0.95. Alpha measures whether the items hang together, not whether the scale measures distress and not whether 28 is the right place to cut it. A HIGH ALPHA ON A NEW SCALE SAYS THE QUESTIONS RESEMBLE EACH OTHER
span.quote: Psychiatrists from the Shanghai Mental Health Center verified the content validity of the CPDI. The Cronbach’s alpha of CPDI is 0.95

span.label: supports → previous research finding women more vulnerable to stress and more likely to develop post-traumatic stress disorder
span.quote: Similarly, people with higher education tended to have more distress, probably because of high self-awareness of their health.

span.label: supports → the effectiveness of the Chinese government's control measures, offered as the explanation for the declining distress curve
span.quote: Results also indicated that as time passes, distress levels among the public have been significantly descending, with the lowest distress level during the Lantern Festival (8 February).

span.label: THE CUT-OFF IS THE FINDING: a score of 28-51 `indicates mild to moderate distress` and >= 52 `indicates severe distress`, asserted without derivation - and `almost 35% experienced psychological distress` IS THAT THRESHOLD restated
span.term: THE CUT-OFF IS THE FINDING: a score of 28-51 `indicates mild to moderate distress` and >= 52 `indicates severe distress`, asserted without derivation - and `almost 35% experienced psychological distress` IS THAT THRESHOLD restated
span.quote: A score between 28 and 51 indicates mild to moderate distress. A score ≥52 indicates severe distress.

span.label: THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE THE SURVEY - the questionnaire was DESIGNED for this epidemic and fielded from the day the WHO declared a PHEIC
span.term: THE INSTRUMENT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE THE SURVEY - the questionnaire was DESIGNED for this epidemic and fielded from the day the WHO declared a PHEIC
span.quote: A self-report questionnaire was designed to survey peritraumatic psychological distress during the epidemic. Data collection began on 31 January 2020, the day when the WHO announced the Novel Coronavirus Pneumonia of China as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

span.label: the validation is content validity plus Cronbach's alpha 0.95 - an internal-consistency statistic, which says the items resemble each other and nothing about where to cut the scale
span.term: the validation is content validity plus Cronbach's alpha 0.95 - an internal-consistency statistic, which says the items resemble each other and nothing about where to cut the scale
span.quote: Psychiatrists from the Shanghai Mental Health Center verified the content validity of the CPDI. The Cronbach’s alpha of CPDI is 0.95
